open_issues: The WebView2 PrintToPdf fallback itself still has no automated test (supervisor ruling 5); only the HTML it prints is tested — now including the letterhead area, the floating blocks, the collapsed padding and the single occurrence of every value.

IDerivedDocumentBuilder and ILetterDocumentStore remain unregistered in App.xaml.cs because the vault belongs to B3-2; TemplateService's optional ILetterDocumentStore resolves to null, so a fresh installation composes on the built-in template.

No NuGet package added; Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx and docs/ (apart from the gitignored progress file) untouched; no git write commands run. HIGH — LetterHtmlRenderer printed the template twice and upside down. Root fix: the renderer now has its own reader instead of reusing the composer's walk. New src/Wakeel.Reports/Letters/LetterLayoutReader.cs (a) skips any paragraph under a DocumentFormat.OpenXml.AlternateContentFallback ancestor, so each text box is read once rather than once per mc:Choice/mc:Fallback pair; (b) emits the header parts' paragraphs first and the footer parts' last, whatever order the package stores them in; (c) reads a text box at the paragraph that anchors it, not after it, so the date block is drawn where Word draws it; (d) reads wp:anchor (positionH relativeFrom/posOffset/align plus wp:extent, against the section's pgSz/pgMar) — or, for a template carrying only a VML shape, that shape's style — and classifies each box as LeftBlock, RightBlock or Band. LetterOpenXml.Paragraphs and TextOf are byte-for-byte unchanged, so Compose and Check behave exactly as before (the conformance test against the owner's filled example is still green). Core gained LetterTemplatePlace, LetterTemplateAlign, LetterTemplateLine and ILetterTemplateInspector.ReadLayout; LetterComposer.RenderHtml now calls ReadLayout. LetterHtmlRenderer.Render emits
above the sheet's flow,
for the floating boxes, a
, honours the template's centring, and collapses a run of consecutive blank template lines to one

(leading and trailing blanks are dropped), so the closing phrase is no longer pushed onto a second page. Verified against the reference template with a scratchpad probe: the printed sheet is letterhead / date-number block floated left / addressee / subject band / greeting / body / one blank / closing phrase / signature block floated left, each exactly once. That also closes the missing spec item (letterhead area, right/left blocks). MEDIUM — TemplateService screened the template only on the way in. ReadLocalCopy now returns null when IsPlainLetterPackage(content) is false, and ReadSetupCopyAsync does the same, so GetAsync falls through to the next source and ultimately to the built-in template. Two tests: a local copy that gained an external attachedTemplate relationship after PrepareLocalCopyAsync wrote it (the file Word edits in place) is ignored and GetAsync returns Origin = BuiltIn; a setup-file copy carrying the same relationship is ignored too. LOW (br/tab) — LetterOpenXml.TextOf is untouched (the composer's splice indexes into it). A separate LetterOpenXml.ReadableTextOf maps w:br to a newline, w:tab to a space and w:noBreakHyphen to a non-breaking hyphen; the layout reader uses it and the renderer emits one

Two tests (docx and HTML) assert no '@' survives when a template line writes @نص المراسلة twice, and that the words after the second mark are still printed. Tests added: 9 (594 total, up from 585).
